clue.text: Unexciting side, with little energy at the last

indicators.note: at the last tells us the energy letter is shifted to the very end of the word for side

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
E is the physics abbreviation for energy, a little bit of the word

explanation.surface: A dull sports team that runs out of steam at the end of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the last' moves the E of TEAM to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexciting is bland and lacking spirit, as a tame story is.

clue.text: Half of team's fixed and ready for assessment

indicators.note: half of points to the first two of the four letters in the word team

parts.note: something fixed in place is stable, firmly settled

explanation.surface: Half the team's line-up is settled, so they are ready to be judged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes TE, the first half of 'team'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something able to be put through a trial or examination is ready for assessment.

clue.text: Mother's attitude upset girl

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for attitude is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude, as in putting on airs

explanation.surface: A mother's manner upsets her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a common female given name, and crosswords use any girl's name for 'girl'.

clue.text: Gamble about contest, initially losing item of jewellery

indicators.note: about means the word for gamble goes around the other letters

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
a race is a contest of speed

indicators.note: initially signals the first letter of the word losing

explanation.surface: A punter bets on a contest and loses their jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the gamble round the contest; 'initially' takes only the opening letter of 'losing', so nothing is lost from the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a band or chain worn round the wrist as an ornament.

clue.text: Sussex town without leader? Exactly so!

indicators.note: without leader says the town's opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on the Sussex coast of southern England

explanation.surface: Someone agrees heartily that a Sussex town has no leader.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a seaside town in Sussex, a county on England's south coast; 'without leader' drops its B.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an informal cry of agreement or approval, like 'Absolutely!'

clue.text: American's to exaggerate a grief involving vegetable — this pest?

parts.note: to colour a story is to exaggerate it, and Americans spell the verb without the U

indicators.note: involving means the word for grief wraps around the vegetable

parts.note: dole is an old poetic word for grief or sorrow, as in doleful
beet is a root vegetable

explanation.surface: An American overstates his sorrow over a vegetable crop ruined by a pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving' splits the grief word after its second letter. Americans spell 'colour' without the U, hence 'American's'; dole as grief survives in 'doleful'.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped beetle is a notorious pest that strips the leaves of potato plants.

clue.text: No replays broadcast for the non-specialist

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A viewer who knows nothing about sport complains that no replays were shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' rearranges NO REPLAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson is someone without professional or expert knowledge of a subject.

clue.text: Wings of the raven or some other bird

indicators.note: wings are the outer parts of a bird, so these are the first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher compares the wings of a raven with those of another bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings of' takes the first and last letters of 'the' and 'raven', TE and RN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tern is a gull-like seabird, so a bird other than the raven.

clue.text: Confused in any department?

explanation.surface: A disoriented shopper wanders into every department of a store.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in total disorder or muddle; read literally it is everywhere in a store, in any department.

clue.text: Artist, important figure, enthralling one

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the important figure holds the other letter inside

parts.note: a titan is a person of great importance or power
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A great artist is a giant who captivates everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enthralling' puts I inside TITAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was a great Venetian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Not a performer in a show that will run and run?

definitions.text: Not a performer in a show that will run and run?

parts.words: Not a performer in a show that will run and run?
parts.note: a long-running show suggests a stage hit, but this actor is one who travels from place to place, so he moves along rather than staying put in one theatre

explanation.surface: An actor who was not cast in a long-running West End hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run and run' suggests a show with a long run; the answer is a travelling actor of old who toured village to village rather than playing one theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically such an actor toured from town to town performing, rather than appearing in one fixed long run.

clue.text: Man is, to a T, dissected — by me?

definitions.text: Man is, to a T, dissected — by me?

indicators.note: dissected means cut apart, so the letters of the phrase before it are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is cut up thoroughly, and the question is who did it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissected' rearranges MAN IS TO A T; the whole clue also describes the answer, the person who cuts up a man to study him.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies bodily structure dissects bodies, so a man is dissected by one.

clue.text: Party — not against a dance

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for against is left out of the word for party

parts.note: a revel is a lively party or celebration
V, from versus, is a common abbreviation for against

explanation.surface: Someone at a party refuses to oppose a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes V (versus, against) from REVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance.

clue.text: Reading-desk shifted centre-left

indicators.note: shifted means moved about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A lectern is moved from the centre to the left of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifted' rearranges CENTRE plus L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a stand with a sloping top that holds a book for someone reading aloud, as in church.

clue.text: Conservative leading remarkably up-to date change of government

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something unusual has been done, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Conservative leads a surprisingly modern change of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' puts C first; 'remarkably' rearranges UPTODATE into OUPDETAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'état is the sudden, often violent, overthrow of a government by a small group.

clue.text: 500 is claimed by eccentric as 'an uncovered figure'

indicators.note: claimed by means taken in by, so the word for eccentric holds the other letters

parts.note: a nut is a crazy or eccentric person
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: An odd figure is said to be worth 500 and described as exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Claimed by' puts the Roman 500 and 'is' inside the eccentric; 'as' is a link, and the quoted definition plays on a figure with no clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes about naked, so is literally a figure without clothing.

clue.text: Danish author with nasty sneer

parts.note: and can mean with, as in fish and chips

indicators.note: nasty suggests something nastily twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Danish writer sneers unpleasantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' rearranges SNEER into ERSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen was the Danish writer of fairy tales such as The Little Mermaid.

clue.text: One caught following deterioration in the country

indicators.note: following places the letters for one and caught after the word for deterioration

parts.note: rust is the corrosion or deterioration of iron
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is arrested after things go downhill in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts I and C after RUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic means rural, belonging to the countryside.

clue.text: Gets to dance in police station

parts.note: to cop is a slang word for get or catch, so cops means gets
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Someone goes off to dance at the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: COP SHOP is informal British slang for a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Cop shop is a slang term for the station where police work.

clue.text: No name given to murder victim back in Middle Eastern country

indicators.note: back means the whole sequence is read backwards

parts.note: in the Bible Abel was murdered by his brother Cain, the first murder victim

explanation.surface: A murder victim goes unnamed back in a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the whole run round at once, so the biblical victim ends up at the front of the country, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a country on the eastern Mediterranean coast, north of Israel.

clue.text: Chap fully rearing woolly creatures

indicators.note: rearing means rising up, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: Sam is a man's name, and any name stands for a chap
all can mean fully, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A man fully raises woolly animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rearing' reverses SAM ALL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American animals with thick woolly fleece.

clue.text: Tidy lawn, trimming front from garden feature

indicators.note: trimming front from cuts off the first letter of the word for a garden feature

parts.note: a hedge is a row of shrubs in a garden

explanation.surface: A gardener tidies the lawn and trims the front of the hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimming front from' cuts the H off HEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge a lawn is to trim its border neatly, a tidying job.

clue.text: Plant in earth, say, next to trimmed water-plant

parts.note: the earth is an example of a planet, signalled by say

indicators.note: trimmed means the end is cut off the word for the water-plant

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing in water

explanation.surface: A gardener plants something in the earth beside a cut-back reed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimmed' takes the D off REED.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane tree is a large deciduous tree with flaking bark, common in city streets.

clue.text: Farm leader deposed from local office

indicators.note: leader deposed from says the first letter is thrown out of the word for a local office

parts.note: a branch is a local office of a bank or firm

explanation.surface: A boss is thrown out of the local office of a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader deposed from' drops the B of BRANCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle in America.

clue.text: Stop article being suppressed by rock group

parts.note: The Who are a British rock band
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A rock band censors a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being suppressed by' puts A inside WHO, the British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is a command to halt, first said to a horse.

clue.text: The Boss put in best-selling song lyrics to get in the news

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the boss goes between the song and its words

parts.note: a hit is a best-selling record
lines are the words of a song
the head is the person in charge, the boss

explanation.surface: Bruce Springsteen, known as The Boss, writes hit lyrics and makes the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in' splits the song from its lyrics. 'The Boss' suggests Bruce Springsteen, but here it is just whoever is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reported prominently in the press is to make the front page of the news.

clue.text: A refusal to accept rebel suggestion from religious rebel

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'A refusal to accept rebel suggestion from religious rebel'. A + NOPE around TIP (suggestion) gives the answer, but the first 'rebel' gives no letters and is no indicator; it looks like an OCR duplication, and no source confirms the printed words.
annotationWithheld.clue: A refusal to accept rebel suggestion from religious rebel

clue.text: Tenuous item getting cut

indicators.note: getting cut means the word for item loses its last letter

parts.note: a thing is an item or object

explanation.surface: An item gets a slim cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting cut' removes the final G of THING.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenuous means slight or flimsy, as a weak argument is.
